articles.title: Why I Choose BEM Over CSS Modules (Most of the Time)
articles.excerpt: CSS architecture is a decision with long-term consequences. Here is why I often reach for BEM methodology over CSS Modules in enterprise codebases.
articles.content:
## The Long-term Impact of CSS Architecture

In large frontend codebases, CSS can easily become a bottleneck. Class name collisions, bloated selectors, and nested cascade paths often make updates risky. While modern frameworks offer encapsulated solutions like **CSS Modules** or **CSS-in-JS**, I frequently find myself choosing the classic **BEM (Block, Element, Modifier)** methodology.

Here is why BEM remains highly practical in large-scale projects, and where encapsulation utilities are best left behind.

---

### 1. Readability and Predictability

With BEM, the class name itself describes the purpose and structure of the styles. 

```css
/* Block */
.card {}

/* Element */
.card__title {}
.card__image {}

/* Modifier */
.card--featured {}
```

When inspecting elements in browser developer tools, BEM classes tell you exactly where the style originates and what relations exist. CSS Modules, on the other hand, generate hashed class names like `_card_1u9z8_5`, making debugging and visual audits much harder for design QA teams.

---

### 2. Zero Build-time Overhead

CSS Modules require specific bundler configurations (Webpack, Vite, Rollup) and JS runtimes to parse and map module tables. BEM is pure vanilla CSS. It works on every platform, every framework, and in static layouts without requiring a compilation step. This makes it perfect for edge environments, server-side rendering, and performance-critical landing pages.

---

### 3. Modifiers are First-Class Citizens

Styling elements dynamically in CSS Modules often results in complex JS template strings:

```javascript
// CSS Modules approach
className={`${styles.card} ${isFeatured ? styles.featured : ''}`}
```

With BEM, modifiers are clean and explicit:

```javascript
// BEM approach
className={`card ${isFeatured ? 'card--featured' : ''}`}
```

---

### Summary Table

| Metric | BEM Methodology | CSS Modules |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Debuggability** | Excellent (clear naming structure) | Hard (hashed class names) |
| **Build dependency** | None (pure CSS) | High (requires bundler plug) |
| **Styles Leakage** | Possible (relic on naming discipline) | Impossible (encapsulated) |
| **Performance** | Maximum (zero parse overhead) | Medium (requires JS mapping) |

While BEM requires discipline from team members to avoid naming violations, its utility, simplicity, and debugging efficiency make it my go-to choice for enterprise CSS architecture.

articles.title: Migrating Large Projects to Nuxt 4
articles.excerpt: Nuxt 4 introduces a restructured directory layout, strict typing, and rendering updates. Here is a migration report and debugging checklist.
articles.content:
## Upgrading Vue Enterprise Projects to Nuxt 4

Migrating enterprise projects is always challenging, particularly when dealing with major version shifts like Nuxt 2 → Nuxt 3, and now the streamlined directory shifts in **Nuxt 4**. 

In my work at IDG, I led migration operations resolving breaking changes and adapting layouts to composition syntax. Here is a checklist of critical factors to watch for.

---

### 1. The Directory Restructure

Nuxt 4 consolidates code files inside a unified `app/` folder structure by default (pages, components, layouts, middleware, composables), leaving configs and public resources in the root.

```bash
# Nuxt 4 structure
├── app/
│   ├── components/
│   ├── layouts/
│   ├── pages/
│   └── app.vue
├── public/
├── server/
├── nuxt.config.ts
└── package.json
```

To preserve the old directory layout during migration, you can configure compatibility mode in `nuxt.config.ts`:

```typescript
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  future: {
    compatibilityVersion: 4
  }
})
```

---

### 2. Smart Component Resolution

Nuxt 4 has updated component autoloading properties. Nested folders now auto-resolve prefixing parent folder names to components. For instance:

- Components inside `components/dashboard/Sidebar.vue` must be called as `<DashboardSidebar />` in views instead of just `<Sidebar />`.

---

### Summary Checklist

- [x] Configure compatibility version variables in configuration files.
- [x] Rename imports referencing nested components to use prefix names.
- [x] Audit global composables: ensure standard imports are explicitly defined.
- [x] Test Server-Side Rendering (SSR) page-load performance and hydrate states.

Migrating early ensures you benefit from Vite's updated hot-reload speeds, reduced build bundle sizes, and optimal TypeScript compilation checks.

articles.title: SETEC Institute MIS Curriculum Breakdown
articles.excerpt: A detailed semester-by-semester breakdown of the Bachelor of Science in Management Information System (MIS) curriculum at SETEC Institute.
articles.content:
## Overview of SETEC Institute's MIS Program The Bachelor of Science in Management Information System (MIS) at SETEC Institute is a comprehensive 4-year degree bridging business management and advanced software engineering. Below is the complete semester-by-semester breakdown. **Click on each course below to see details about what I learnt.** --- ### Year 1: Foundational Sciences & Programming #### Semester 1
A+ (Computer Maintenance & Repair) I

What I learnt: Core hardware components, diagnosis, assembly, and operating systems. Understand motherboard architectures, RAM types, CPU socket configurations, power supplies, troubleshooting hardware post-errors, and installing Windows/Linux OS.

C++ Programming

What I learnt: Procedural programming paradigm, variables, pointers, reference variables, control flow, functions, structures, arrays, and standard libraries (iostream, vector).

Office Applications

What I learnt: Advanced spreadsheet functions (VLOOKUP, INDEX-MATCH, Pivot Tables), formatting technical reports, and building slide decks.

Data Structure I

What I learnt: Static and dynamic linear data structures. Implemented stacks, queues, and singly/doubly linked lists in C++.

History

What I learnt: Global and local socio-economic history, formatting historical context analyses.

Principles of Management

What I learnt: Organizational planning, directing, decision-making frameworks, SWOT analysis, and management roles.

Computer Mathematics

What I learnt: Discrete mathematics, set theory, boolean algebra, logic gates, and graph theory.

Graphic Design I

What I learnt: Color theory, grid alignments, raster image editing with Adobe Photoshop, and page layout guidelines.

English 1

What I learnt: Grammar rules, business letter formats, and oral presentations.

#### Semester 2
A+ (Computer Maintenance & Repair) II

What I learnt: Diagnostic software, hardware benchmarking, assembling network cards, and electrical safety standards for workstations.

C# Programming I

What I learnt: Basic C# syntax, variables, class declarations, encapsulation, access modifiers, constructors, and properties on .NET framework.

Web Development I

What I learnt: HTML5 layout tags, CSS3 selectors, responsive layouts using media queries, and basic DOM manipulation with vanilla JavaScript.

Data Structure II

What I learnt: Non-linear structures, binary search trees (BST), graph traversal algorithms (DFS, BFS), sorting algorithms (Quicksort, Mergesort).

Culture & Civilisation

What I learnt: Evolution of human cultures, ethics in society, and philosophical frameworks.

Public Relations

What I learnt: Creating press releases, crisis management communications, public campaigns, and brand reputation methods.

Accounting

What I learnt: Double-entry bookkeeping system, journaling transactions, ledger balancing, and creating balance sheets.

Graphic Design II

What I learnt: Vector graphics editing with Adobe Illustrator, anchor points, pen tool techniques, and logo design layouts.

English 2

What I learnt: Academic essay writing, documentation standards, and argumentative speeches.

--- ### Year 2: Systems, Networks & Web Tech #### Semester 3
Networking I

What I learnt: OSI Reference Model, TCP/IP protocol suite, subnetting IPv4 addresses, and configuring basic switches/routers.

C# Programming II

What I learnt: OOP in C#: inheritance, interface implementation, custom exceptions, delegates, events, and garbage collection mechanisms.

Web Development II

What I learnt: Server-side rendering (PHP/Node.js), connecting forms to database backends, sessions, and cookies.

Data Modeling & Relational DBase Design

What I learnt: Entity-Relationship Diagrams (ERD), normalization rules (1NF, 2NF, 3NF), mapping relationships, and referential integrity constraints.

Database Server Applications I

What I learnt: Microsoft SQL Server administration, creating tables, primary/foreign keys, joins, subqueries, and writing complex select queries.

Studio Photography I

What I learnt: Camera settings (aperture, shutter speed, ISO), exposure triangle, composition rules, and basic editing.

Computer Accounting

What I learnt: Running ledger sheets, inventory lists, client invoices, and financial audits inside software packages like QuickBooks.

Graphic Design III

What I learnt: Multi-page layouts (Adobe InDesign), brand guidelines, print preflight operations, and PDF publishing.

UX/UI (User Experience/User Interface)

What I learnt: User personas, user journey mapping, high-fidelity wireframing with Figma, component variants, and interactive prototyping.

#### Semester 4
Networking II

What I learnt: Switch port security, VLAN routing, Spanning Tree Protocol (STP), and EtherChannel configurations.

C# Programming III

What I learnt: Desktop UI layouts with WPF/WinForms, asynchronous programming (async/await), and data access using ADO.NET / Entity Framework Core.

Web Development III

What I learnt: Dynamic Web applications, authentication systems (session tokens), basic security (XSS, CSRF defense), and server deployment.

Drawing Skills for Multimedia

What I learnt: Linear perspective, basic anatomy drawing, storyboard layouts, and shading dynamics.

Database Server Application II

What I learnt: Stored procedures, user-defined functions, transaction controls, triggers, and query execution plans.

Studio Photography II

What I learnt: Product mockups, studio strobe configurations, flash ratios, and advanced photo retouching in Adobe Lightroom.

Studio Multimedia I

What I learnt: Audio capture/editing, video timelines, transitions, keyframes, and exports in Adobe Premiere.

3D Graphic Design

What I learnt: Polygonal modeling, mesh subdivisions, material textures, lighting configurations, and rendering in Blender/3ds Max.

Applied Computer Design

What I learnt: Combining text, vector art, 3D renders, and animation layouts into interactive web/desktop client presentations.

--- ### Year 3: Advanced Software Engineering & Specialized Fields #### Semester 5
Networking III

What I learnt: Configuring routing protocols (OSPF, EIGRP), WAN connections, and network management tools (SNMP).

Java Programming I

What I learnt: Java language structures, JVM, byte code execution, object instantiation, basic collections (ArrayList, HashMap).

Web Based Development I

What I learnt: MVC architecture, front-controllers, template engines, and building database-driven web platforms.

Introduction to Oracle I

What I learnt: Oracle Database architecture, tablespaces, user privilege controls, and SQL*Plus scripts.

Management Information System

What I learnt: IT systems in business operations, enterprise resource planning (ERP) configurations, decision support systems (DSS), and data warehouses.

Animation 2D

What I learnt: Traditional animation rules (squash/stretch, staging), timeline framing, and motion tweening in Adobe Animate.

Studio Multimedia II

What I learnt: Interactive web multimedia scripts, video rendering formats, and high-fidelity video production workflows.

System Analysis I

What I learnt: Software development processes (Waterfall, Agile), gathering functional/non-functional requirements, use-case diagrams, and class diagrams.

Interviewing Skills

What I learnt: Writing professional cover letters, standard resume formatting, body language, and behavioral interview methods.

#### Semester 6
Configuring Network Devices I

What I learnt: Advanced routing configurations, Access Control Lists (ACLs) for security, and Network Address Translation (NAT) deployment.

Java Programming II

What I learnt: Advanced OOP in Java, abstract classes, multi-threaded programming, socket connections, and database integration (JDBC).

Web Based Development II

What I learnt: Modern web frameworks (Vue.js, Laravel), RESTful API endpoint designs, middleware interceptors, and CORS settings.

Introduction to Oracle II

What I learnt: Writing PL/SQL blocks, local variables, cursors, custom functions, procedures, database packages, and system triggers.

Python Programming

What I learnt: Python script syntax, list comprehensions, script-based file automation, API fetching, and introduction to pip.

Computer Animation I

What I learnt: Vector character design, skeletal joints, inverse kinematics, and animating short stories.

Mobile Application I

What I learnt: Android SDK basics, XML UI layouts, activity lifecycles, and intent actions.

System Analysis II

What I learnt: Designing data flow diagrams (DFD), system interfaces, system testing methods (Unit, Integration, UAT), and software architectural patterns.

Linux System Administration I

What I learnt: Linux terminal navigation, shell file permissions, user group administration, package management (APT/YUM), and bash scripting.

--- ### Year 4: Advanced Systems, Integration & Career #### Semester 7
Configuring Network Devices II

What I learnt: VPN architectures (IPsec/GRE), network redundancy protocols (HSRP), and edge firewall policies.

Java Programming III

What I learnt: Enterprise Java (Jakarta EE), Spring Framework (Spring Boot, Spring Data JPA, Spring Security), and deploying APIs to Docker container environments.

Web Projects

What I learnt: Agile project lifecycle, building full-stack web applications in teams, task scheduling, git branches, and live deployments.

Ethics & Law of IT

What I learnt: Intellectual property laws, copyright agreements, cybersecurity acts, privacy rules (GDPR), and professional ACM ethics code.

Advanced Python Programming

What I learnt: Data analysis pipelines (Pandas, NumPy), data visualizations (Matplotlib), and basics of predictive machine learning models.

Computer Animation II

What I learnt: Special effects layers, green-screen compositing, and rendering advanced sequences.

Mobile Application II

What I learnt: Native iOS development (SwiftUI) and cross-platform UI frameworks (Flutter/React Native).

E-Commerce

What I learnt: Payment checkout logic (KHQR/Bakong, Stripe), shopping cart sessions, SSL certificates, and transactional database safety.

Linux System Administration II

What I learnt: Hardening Linux servers, configuring firewalls (iptables/ufw), DNS services, Nginx reverse proxies, and system logging.

#### Semester 8
Student Internship Program or Research (Thesis)

What I learnt: Practical on-site software engineering, integrating code into large codebases, resolving merchant bugs, and writing structured research project logs.

Career Placement Program

What I learnt: Building digital portfolios, professional networking on LinkedIn, and mock interview preparations.
